title: Energy And Grid Capacity: From System Forecast To Named Service
summary: Follow national storage growth into named plant-code panels, energy duration, availability, dispatch, safety, revenue, grid service, and customer reliability.
current_state_summary: Moss Landing, Manatee, and Gateway now have three-year EIA-860 nameplate power-capacity panels keyed to stable plant codes.
current_state: Data-centre electricity growth is visible as a system constraint, but no global or national forecast proves local spare capacity.
EIA's 2025 Form 860 early release and 2026 Form 923 update distinguish generator status from observed plant output; neither proves customer-level deliverable capacity.
SRP's E-67 tariff identifies service conditions, while Project Huckleberry records a separate named infrastructure project that reached service for Meta in Mesa.
APS identifies TSMC in its service territory and reports rapid utility-wide demand growth without disclosing customer load, infrastructure, energization, or spare capacity.
DOE's Southline capacity contract creates a trackable transmission project without proving construction or energization.
Ontario's provincial outlook and Toronto distribution proceeding expose layered planning without resolving any project's connection.
Project Pele's delivered TRISO fuel and DOE's storage prize reach physical and production-readiness stages without proving grid operation.
EIA reports 11 hours of average customer interruption in 2024, with major events responsible for 80 percent of the duration.
NERC reports Texas batteries supplied up to all frequency-regulation capacity in several 2024 instances and more than 70 percent of response in individual disturbances.
EIA reports utility-scale battery power capacity rising from 4,605 MW at the end of 2021 to 15,814 MW at the end of 2023.
EIA's outage-duration series shows why major-event and non-major-event customer experience must remain separate.
Plant code 260 rises from 400 MW to 750 MW by 2023; plant codes 60014 and 63834 retain 409 MW and 250 MW, respectively, across the three final vintages.
The panels measure nameplate power only and do not rank asset performance.
Phase 56C adds entity-matched controls, inputs, constraints, later observations, attribution, independent-validation limits, and alternative explanations.
Temporal order is preserved without converting association into causation, ranking, composite scoring, or readiness scoring.
Phase 56D adds later observations and explicit tests of named Phase 56C alternative explanations for the same twelve entities.
Compatibility, attribution, validation status, missing denominators, and series breaks remain visible before any interpretation.
Phase 56E adds a second vertically replicated cohort: Hornsdale Power Reserve, Victorian Big Battery, Dalrymple ESCRI-SA Battery Energy Storage System.
Every retained entity carries a panel, a driver-and-constraint dossier, and an alternative-explanation test under one stable identity.
Phase 56F assigns every entity one highest-value missing record, one strongest compatible current record, a closure state, and an explicit reopening rule.
Across all 24 entities, one bounded record is Closed, sixteen are Partially Closed, and seven remain Open; these are evidence states, not performance measures.
Phase 56G checked 4 exact record rails in this pathway and retained the Phase 56F reopening rules.
Dalrymple now has a later asset-specific control-scheme record; actual events and operating denominators remain open.
Phase 56H checked 5 named records in this pathway against existing coverage IDs and continuation rules.
1 selected evidence state advances from Open to Partially Closed; the remaining denominators stay explicit.
Phase 56I completes 2 first-pass decisions in this pathway while retaining each coverage ID and continuation rule.
No selected closure state changes; genuinely new denominators publish and repeated evidence remains referenced rather than relabeled as a new finding.
Phase 56J adds 3 named continuation decisions to this pathway under the ordered evidence-value queue.
Acquisition order describes evidence opportunity and does not rank entities, performance, safety, quality, readiness, or value.
Phase 56K checks 2 exact named records in this pathway and preserves explicit non-closures.
An exact-record check can improve the evidence rail without changing the selected closure state.
Phase 56P adds five exact DOE actions across nuclear modernization, environmental liabilities, energy security, and program management.

evidence_limits: The pathway does not convert global, national, or provincial electricity forecasts into local service capacity.
One named Meta service project cannot establish transferability to TSMC, another data centre, housing growth, or a different utility territory.
Identifying APS as TSMC's serving utility closes a location question, not the customer-capacity, infrastructure, energization, or operation question.
Transmission and prize awards do not prove construction, manufacturing readiness, energization, commercial terms, or operating performance.
The Ontario record remains upstream of project-level feeder, transformer, station, connection, construction, and energization evidence.
Battery power capacity, energy duration, dispatch, availability, frequency response, and customer reliability are different measures.
Bulk-power performance and distribution customer outcomes remain separate system layers.
Observation dates, major-event treatment, survey revisions, and utility reporting coverage govern comparison.
EIA can revise plant names, generator status, ownership, and capacity in later annual vintages.
A named intervention, control, input, or response does not by itself explain an observed outcome.
Company and operator claims remain attributed until independently validated.
A recommendation status, certification, supplier clause, incident response, monthly cause mix, or complaint count does not create a common performance measure.
Different units, methods, identities, observation windows, and attribution levels remain split.
The second cohort preserves attribution, unit, denominator, method, observation window, reporting breaks, and identity changes.
A vertical entity record does not authorize cross-entity ranking, composite scoring, readiness scoring, or causal inference.
Phase 56F closure states apply to one named missing record per entity and cannot be converted into a ranking, composite, readiness score, or causal claim.
Phase 56G acquisition outcomes measure evidence closure only and cannot be converted into entity performance, a comparison, or a score.
Phase 56H closure and deepening states cannot be converted into rankings, scores, readiness, quality, safety, value, or causal claims.
Phase 56I first-pass and closure states cannot be converted into rankings, scores, readiness, quality, safety, value, or causal claims.
Phase 56J acquisition order and closure states cannot be converted into rankings, scores, readiness, quality, safety, value, or causal claims.
Phase 56K exact-record decisions cannot be converted into rankings, scores, readiness, quality, safety, value, or causal claims.
Cost estimates, analyses, reviews, oversight, and pause conditions do not establish project completion, cleanup savings, reserve adequacy, or service outcomes.
FTFN Phase 56P action keys are stable local references, not official GAO Recommendations Database numbers.
